app.name: Slack
app.canDo: Post messages and replies. Read channel history and threads to summarise, search or sort them.

verdict.summary: To post messages, you can make the app yourself in minutes. To read messages at a useful rate, you need a Slack Marketplace listing. New unlisted apps can read history only one time each minute, 15 messages at a time.

whoYouNeed.role: A member of a Slack workspace that you control
whoYouNeed.why: You create each Slack app in one workspace. You test the app there first.

whoYouNeed.role: 10 or more real customer workspaces (for reading messages)
whoYouNeed.why: Slack reviews a Marketplace app only after it has 10 active installs.

steps.title: Sign in to the Slack app dashboard
steps.plain: Sign in at api.slack.com/apps with the workspace that will own the app.

evidence.note: Div did this by hand on 2026-10-29.

steps.title: Create the app from a pre-filled link
steps.plain: This link opens the Slack 'Create app' screen. The usual agent permissions are already on it. Change the name, select your workspace and remove the permissions that you do not need. Then click Create and Install.

evidence.note: Div did this by hand on 2026-10-29. Our first link had no bot user, and Slack showed 'We can't translate a manifest with errors'. The link is now fixed.

steps.technical: The link uses the Slack manifest URL (`api.slack.com/apps?new_app=1&manifest_json=...`). It adds these bot scopes: `chat:write`, `channels:read`, `channels:history`, `users:read`, and a bot user. Slack rejects a manifest with bot scopes and no bot user. Create and Install also installs the app in your own workspace, and Slack then shows a bot token (`xoxb-`). Do not paste that token into an agent chat. You add your callback address in the next step.

link.label: Create the app with settings pre-filled

steps.title: Examine the callback address and permissions
steps.plain: Open OAuth & Permissions. Add the callback address of your app as a redirect URL. Make sure that the permissions are the ones that your agent needs.
steps.technical: Redirect URLs must use HTTPS. They cannot contain '#'. Slack shows bot scopes and user scopes in two lists.

evidence.note: Div did this by hand on 2026-10-29. Remember to click Save URLs. The Manage Distribution page shows a reminder until a redirect URL is saved.

link.label: Open your app, then OAuth & Permissions

steps.title: Turn on public distribution
steps.plain: If you do not do this step, only your workspace can install the app. Open Manage Distribution. Complete each item on the Slack checklist. Click Activate Public Distribution.
steps.technical: The checklist has four items: Enable Features & Functionality, Add OAuth redirect URLs, Remove hard-coded information (you tick a box to confirm), and Use HTTPS for your features. Slack does not review the app at this step.

evidence.note: Div did this by hand on 2026-10-29. Div saw the four-item checklist.

link.label: Open your app, then Manage Distribution

steps.title: Keep the client ID and secret in your app
steps.plain: Open Basic Information. Copy the client ID and client secret into the secret store or environment variables of your app.
steps.whyHuman: The secret is the password for your app. Paste it yourself. Then it does not go into the chat history of an agent.

evidence.note: Div did this by hand on 2026-10-29.

steps.title: Install in a second workspace to test
steps.plain: Install the app in a different workspace through the sign-in of your app. This shows that other teams can install it.

evidence.note: On 2026-10-29 Div installed the app through its own sign-in link, in the same workspace. The consent screen showed the app name and the two permissions, and Slack sent the browser to the callback address. A second workspace was not tested. Slack tells Marketplace applicants to test outside the development workspace. We give the same advice here.

steps.title: Get 10 active workspaces (reading only)
steps.plain: At least 10 workspaces must install and use the app in the last 28 days. Until then, you cannot apply for the Marketplace. Also, new installs can read only slowly.
steps.whyHuman: These must be real customers or pilots. Your own test workspaces do not count.

steps.title: Send the app to the Slack Marketplace (reading only)
steps.plain: Send the app from its settings. Include a demo video that shows install, sign-in, use and uninstall. Include a test account with test data. Tell why you need each permission.
steps.whyHuman: A person must make the video and the test account. An agent can write a draft of the reasons for each permission.

link.label: Open your app, then Submit to Slack Marketplace

steps.title: Slack reviews your app (reading only)
steps.plain: The first review takes a maximum of 10 business days. Then the functional review of a new app takes a maximum of 10 weeks. If you send the app again during the first review, you go back to the end of the queue.

evidence.note: Slack gives only maximum times. The minimum of 14 days is our estimate.

forks.effect: Stop after step 6. The limits apply only when you read history and threads. Thus, you do not need a Marketplace listing.

sources.title: Slack changelog: rate limits for non-Marketplace apps

nuances.title: Unlisted apps read Slack slowly
nuances.detail: Since May 29, 2025, Slack limits commercial apps outside the Marketplace. They get 1 request each minute and a maximum of 15 messages in each call to conversations.history and conversations.replies. Internal apps keep 50 or more requests each minute and 1,000 messages.
nuances.ifStuck: For pilots, read only recent messages. Or, install the app as an internal app in the workspace of each customer. For many customers, start the Marketplace listing early.

sources.title: Slack changelog: rate limits for non-Marketplace apps

evidence.note: The Slack changelog says that the limits do not apply to existing installs of older apps. Other sources say that the Slack FAQ applies the limits to existing installs from March 3, 2026. We did not find this on a Slack page.

nuances.title: For your own workspace, you may not need OAuth
nuances.detail: Create and Install puts the app in your workspace and shows a bot token at once. That token is enough for your own workspace. You need the OAuth steps only when other workspaces install your app.
nuances.ifStuck: Keep the bot token in your secret store. Do not paste it into an agent chat.

evidence.note: Div did this by hand on 2026-10-29.

nuances.title: The callback address must be HTTPS
nuances.detail: Slack does not accept callback addresses that start with http://. This is also true for local tests.
nuances.ifStuck: Use an HTTPS address. For local work, use a tunnel, for example ngrok.

nuances.title: Ask for fewer permissions
nuances.detail: Workspace admins look at the permissions that your app requests. They use this to decide if they approve your app.
nuances.ifStuck: Remove the scopes that your agent does not use now. You can add them later.

config.redirectUriNote: Add the HTTPS callback address of your app in OAuth & Permissions > Redirect URLs.

scopes.name: channels:history
scopes.plain: Read messages in the public channels that the app is in.

scopes.name: groups:history
scopes.plain: Read messages in the private channels that the app is in.

useCases.label: Post messages and replies
useCases.summary: Create the app and turn on public distribution. Slack does not review the app. Do steps 1 to 6.

useCases.label: Read channel history or threads (summaries, search, triage)
useCases.summary: Slack limits unlisted apps that you created after May 29, 2025. They get 1 request each minute and 15 messages in each request to conversations.history and conversations.replies. To remove the limit, you need a Marketplace listing. First, get 10 or more active installs. Then the review takes a maximum of 10 business days and then a maximum of 10 weeks.

sources.title: Slack changelog: rate limits for non-Marketplace apps

useCases.label: Only in the workspace of your company
useCases.summary: Slack does not limit internal apps. They need no distribution and no review.

sources.title: Slack changelog: rate limits for non-Marketplace apps

version.note: This is not OAuth 1.0a. You do not sign each request.

flow.note: Your server exchanges the code for a token at `oauth.v2.access`.

pkce.note: Turn on `pkce_enabled`. The app becomes a public client, and you cannot undo this. Refresh tokens then expire after 30 days.

callback.note: The address must use HTTPS. It cannot contain #.

tokens.note: This changes if you turn on token rotation.

state.note: If it does not match, treat the sign-in as a forgery.

composio.note: Users can connect today through the Composio Slack app. Use it while you set up your own app or wait for the review. Users see 'Composio' on the approval screen. Other Composio customers share the same rate limits. Polling triggers run a maximum of one time in 15 minutes. Change to your own app when it is ready.

limits.note: The Composio Slack app is not on the Marketplace yet. Composio says that its review continues. Thus, it has the same limits as each unlisted app when it reads history. It gets a maximum of 15 messages in each request. It does not let you read without the wait.

existingApp.summary: If the callback address of your agent is different, add it in OAuth & Permissions. Use the existing client ID and secret. Existing installs continue to work.

reReviewTriggers.effect: New scopes apply only after each workspace installs the app again.

reReviewTriggers.trigger: Your app is on the Slack Marketplace and you change permissions
reReviewTriggers.effect: Send the app for review again. For published apps, the functional review takes a maximum of 6 weeks.

reReviewTriggers.trigger: Your app is unlisted and gets new installs
reReviewTriggers.effect: Slack limits installs after May 29, 2025 when they read history. This is also true if the app is older.

sources.title: Slack changelog: rate limits for non-Marketplace apps

blockers.symptom: Slack does not let you send the app to the Marketplace
blockers.cause: An app must have at least 10 active workspace installs before you can send it.
blockers.fix: Give your install link directly to customer workspaces. When you have 10 active installs, send the app.

blockers.symptom: Slack sends back your Marketplace application
blockers.cause: These are the usual causes: scopes for features that you did not build, scopes without a good reason, install problems, or bugs that stop tests. Reviewers cannot get into your workspaces.
blockers.fix: Correct each item of the feedback in your app settings. Then send the app again. Request only the scopes that you use now. Give reviewers a test account and a method to install the app. If you send the app again during the first review, you go back to the end of the queue.

blockers.symptom: A customer cannot install your app
blockers.cause: The workspace of the customer needs admin approval for apps. Or, the workspace blocks your app.
blockers.fix: Tell the customer to request the app. A workspace owner or app manager must approve it. Users cannot request a blocked app.

sources.title: Slack: Manage app approval for your workspace
